subject: Conditional log disposition exception for AdaptiveCare – granularity & proof
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <e.zhang@adaptivecare.io>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.khan@adaptivecare.io>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary carveout to 180d retention for session-forensics logs

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the quick intro call this morning. Following up in writing so my security team has a single thread to track. AdaptiveCare is going through a product-integrations audit (SOC 2 in Q4) and we have a specific ask related to session-level forensic logs that impact a pilot we plan to run in July.

Scope and ask (high level):
- Current Redwood default: 30d ephemeral session logs (session_kv, convo_metadata, routing traces).
- Our need: retain a narrow subset of session-forensics artifacts for 180 days for investigative purposes tied to patient-support incidents. This subset would be limited to: session identifiers, timestamps, routing traces, and error stack traces where user-reported incidents exist. Not full user payloads.

Why: regulators we work with require a 6-month window for incident follow-up during pilot phases; our legal/compliance team is willing to accept a narrowly-scoped carveout with compensating controls.

Deliverables we need from Redwood to approve:
1) A short technical description of which log fields you can preserve for 180d and which will still be deleted at 30d.
2) Evidence of access controls/audit logs showing only AdaptiveCare principals and Redwood security operations have access to the retained subset.
3) An export sample (redacted) of the retained log format so our SOC team can confirm non-PII.
4) Proposed language for a short amendment to our contract (we prefer a 30–90 day implementation/deployment timeline).

I've attached our completed SIG-lite for the pilot and a small sample of the log records (redacted) we need to map to your fields. Please let me know if you need a formal SIG/CAIQ or if the attached CSV is sufficient.

We appreciate a pragmatic path here — happy to limit to a single test tenant.

Thanks,
Emily Zhang\Director, Security & Privacy\AdaptiveCare

Attachments: adaptivecare_SIG_export.csv (CSV), log-sample-2027-05-20.zip (redacted logs)

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Emily Zhang <e.zhang@adaptivecare.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary carveout to 180d retention for session-forensics logs

Emily —

Thanks for the clear ask and the sample files, this is the right level of detail for us to start. We're open to a narrowly-scoped, tenant-scoped retention carveout provided we have compensating controls and clear technical constraints documented.

Quick clarifying questions so we scope correctly:
- When you say "routing traces" do you mean only service-level hops / headers (no user content)?
- For "error stack traces" — are you asking to retain full stack payloads or just error IDs + timestamps?
- Confirm: carveout applies only to one test tenant (tenant_id to be provided), not to all AdaptiveCare tenants.

Next steps from Redwood side (proposal):
1) Security evidence packet: access-control screenshots, audit-log samples showing RBAC, and a short runbook describing who can approve exports.
2) Technical mapping: a table mapping AdaptiveCare CSV columns to Redwood internal log fields and retention TTL per field. We can provide a redacted sample export (JSON-lines) for your SOC review.
3) Implementation plan & timeline: configuration changes, validation run, and a 30–60 day rollback/test window.

Looping in Marissa (security evidence) and Jonas (platform) to own the artifact and the technical mapping. Neha — can you validate whether we can meet 180d for the limited field set and comment on storage/quantization impact?

I'll draft suggested amendment language once we confirm fields and controls.

—Olga
Olga Petrov\Senior Security & Compliance Manager\Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Emily Zhang <e.zhang@adaptivecare.io>, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary carveout to 180d retention for session-forensics logs

Emily / team —

Summary of our assessment and proposed approach:

1) Field-level mapping (we will produce a CSV mapping as a deliverable):
- session_id -> retained (180d)
- session_start_ts, session_end_ts -> retained (180d)
- routing_hops_metadata -> retained (180d) but truncated to headers only (no body/payload)
- error_id, error_timestamp -> retained (180d)
- error_stack (full) -> NOT retained beyond 30d; we can retain error_hash + short snippet (first 256 chars) for 180d if you confirm that satisfies your downstream analysis.
- user_message_payloads, user_personal_data -> NOT retained beyond 30d (we will redact/strip before anything is persisted to the longer window)

2) Access controls and audit evidence:
- We will produce audit snapshots (read-only) showing RBAC entries, and a sample CloudTrail/Audit export demonstrating that only AdaptiveCare service principals and a named Redwood SRE read-only account were used to retrieve the 180d subset during a test run.
- Compensating controls we propose: tenant-scoped key wrapping (KMS) for the retained subset + enforced export approval workflow requiring two Redwood approvers for production exports.

3) Technical feasibility & impact:
- Storage/compute: retaining the reduced field set for one tenant at 180d is low impact (<0.8% of a single model host's disk assuming our typical session volume). We estimate a one-off config flag and a small schema migration in our log-store (2–3 sprint-days).
- Implementation ETA: we can deliver a test deployment in 3 weeks, and production toggle in 5 weeks after sign-off. We can target a 30–45 day rollout if your timeline needs to be faster.

4) Evidence package and amendment language (next deliverables):
- Package: CSV field mapping, redacted JSON-lines export, RBAC/audit snapshots (PDF), proposed amendment text (DocuSign link stub).
- We'll mark all artifacts with a canonical evidence_id and store them in a restricted Drive folder; access will be logged.

Attached: preliminary redacted export (log-sample-2027-05-20.zip) and a short checklist we use for evidentiary handoffs.

If Emily confirms you only need the error_hash + snippet rather than full stack traces, we can proceed without elevating risk.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole\Security Evidence Lead\Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence-checklist.pdf (stub), log-sample-2027-05-20.zip (redacted)

From: Emily Zhang <e.zhang@adaptivecare.io>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, Samir Khan <samir.khan@adaptivecare.io>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 14:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary carveout to 180d retention for session-forensics logs

Hi Marissa / Olga —

This mapping looks good and matches our SOC reviewer expectations. Confirmation on two bullets:
- We accept keeping only error_hash + first 256 chars of stack for the 180d window (no full payloads).
- Tenant-scoped KMS + two-approver export workflow satisfies our compensating control ask.

Next ask from our side: can Redwood provide the proposed amendment language as a DocuSign-ready doc (we'll route through our legal) and also provide the redacted JSON-lines sample in the Drive folder you mentioned so our SOC reviewer can run a quick schema validation?

If you can have the amendment draft and evidence pack in the Drive link by next Wednesday (2027-06-30), we can keep the pilot deadline. Otherwise we'll ask for a short timeline extension.

Thanks — appreciate the pragmatic path.
Emily Zhang\Director, Security & Privacy\AdaptiveCare
